title: One-step register decrement
statement: Let $P$ be a counter program with 11 registers, let $x$ be a binary input, and let $ho$ be the register assignment encoded by an environment $e$. If the instruction at label $$ decrements register $r$ and jumps to label $'$, then for every current output string $o$, there is a run of at most one step from label $$ with registers $ho$ and input position $p$ to label $'$, with register assignment obtained by reducing register $r$ by one (leaving it at zero if it was zero), input position still $p$, and output still $o$.
hypotheses_covered: The input is a binary list
The starting label is $$ and the destination label is $'$
The register assignment is the one encoded by $e$
The instruction at $$ decrements register $r$ and jumps to $'$
The run is bounded by one step and applies for every starting output string
